corrects.what_was_incomplete: it concluded the population was 'not reproducible', which is true of every mutable store and was read as though the population were lost
corrects.what_is_added: the sealed population was never lost — it is PRESERVED as a materialized artifact, in two independent copies

SEALED_HISTORICAL_POPULATION.answers: which episodes were actually in the frozen historical population?

CURRENT_STORE_RECONSTRUCTION.rule: the historical population must be CONSUMED from the preserved artifact, never regenerated from a mutable store

checks.check: row count equals the sealed population
episode_id RECOMPUTES from (ticker, t1_date) through the generator
the generator's definition hash is the one the sealed estimand names
prev_session_date is populated for every episode
the archived copy has the same row count
the two copies are content-identical on the identity grain
the 15m estimand population is preserved at its sealed size
every estimand episode_id is a member of the episode population

verification.why_recomputation_matters: a file with the right row count can still be the wrong file; recomputing episode_id through the generator ties the population to the definition hash

consumption_rule.bind: data/t1_episodes.parquet by sha256 and identity content hash
consumption_rule.do_not: re-run the episode SQL against any mutable store and treat the result as the historical population
consumption_rule.expected_count_forbidden: 220,351 must not be used as a target for any Massive build; it describes the historical population only

enumeration_backing.note: this artifact is written against a completed enumeration, so its statements about what exists rest on a measured search space
